importantNotes: The Davidic Covenant (ch. 7) is fulfilled ultimately in Jesus Christ.
David's sin with Bathsheba shows that no one is beyond temptation.
Nathan's confrontation of David ('You are the man!') is a model for speaking truth to power.
David's repentance (Psalm 51) shows genuine contrition before God.
The family turmoil (Amnon, Absalom) shows that sin's consequences ripple through generations.

chapters.1: David mourns the deaths of Saul and Jonathan; his lament 'How the mighty have fallen.'
chapters.2: David is anointed king over Judah; civil war between David's forces and Ish-Bosheth's.
chapters.3: Abner defects to David but is killed by Joab; David mourns Abner.
chapters.4: Ish-Bosheth is assassinated; David punishes his murderers.
chapters.5: David becomes king over all Israel; he conquers Jerusalem and makes it his capital.
chapters.6: David brings the Ark of the Covenant to Jerusalem with dancing and celebration.
chapters.7: God's covenant with David — his throne will be established forever.
chapters.8: David's military victories expand Israel's borders; his administration.
chapters.9: David shows kindness to Mephibosheth, Jonathan's crippled son.
chapters.10: War against the Ammonites and Arameans after David's ambassadors are humiliated.
chapters.11: David commits adultery with Bathsheba and arranges the death of her husband Uriah.
chapters.12: Nathan confronts David; the child born from the affair dies; Solomon is born.
chapters.13: Amnon assaults his half-sister Tamar; Absalom kills Amnon in revenge.
chapters.14: Joab arranges for Absalom's return to Jerusalem through a wise woman's parable.
chapters.15: Absalom launches a rebellion and takes the throne; David flees Jerusalem.
chapters.16: Shimei curses David; Absalom takes his father's concubines publicly.
chapters.17: Hushai's counsel defeats Ahithophel's advice; Ahithophel hangs himself.
chapters.18: David's forces defeat Absalom's army; Absalom is killed by Joab against David's orders.
chapters.19: David mourns Absalom and is restored to the throne; internal tensions remain.
chapters.20: Sheba's rebellion is put down by Joab; David's officials are listed.
chapters.21: A famine caused by Saul's treatment of the Gibeonites; battles with Philistine giants.
chapters.22: David's song of praise — 'The LORD is my rock, my fortress and my deliverer.'
chapters.23: David's last words; the exploits of David's mighty warriors.
chapters.24: David's census and its consequences; he purchases the threshing floor of Araunah.
